sattapaṇṇiguhā.notes: DN 16:3.42.3 places the cave on Vebhāra. SN 1.20 takes place at the hot springs at Tapodārāma and does not mention the cave.

sayha.notes: MN 116:6.22 names Sayha among the independent Buddhas of Isigili. Asayha appears separately two lines earlier.

sañjaya.notes: MN 36 and MN 77 give the teacher's patronymic Belaṭṭhaputta. DN 2, DN 16, MN 30, SN 3.1, SN 44.9 and Snp 3.6 spell his name Sañcaya, which has a separate DPD lemma. DN 1 describes evasive teachers anonymously, and the AN 5.286–302 citation does not name him. In MN 90 Viḍūḍabha identifies the Ākāsa brahmin in answer to Pasenadi. Thag 1.48 attributes the verse to the elder. Thag 1.50 is Vimala's verse, with Sañjaya in the closing list of elders.

sañjikāputta.notes: In MN 85 Prince Bodhi sends the student Sañjikāputta to invite the Buddha and the Saṅgha to the meal at Kokanada.

sañjīva.notes: MN 50 recounts the attempt to cremate Kakusandha's disciple during meditation. DN 14:1.9.4 and SN 15.20:2.8 also name him in vidhurasañjīvaṁ, the compound for the pair of chief disciples, which has its own dictionary line. The packet has no entry for the hell.

saṅgharakkhita.notes: Thag 1.109 attributes the deer simile to the elder. Thag 1.110:2.5 repeats his name in the chapter recap as Saṅgharakkhitatthero.

saṅgārava.notes: AN 5.193 and SN 46.55 give Saṅgārava's question about remembering hymns. The entry also covers the student at Caṇḍalakappa in MN 100 and the bath ritualist at Sāvatthī in SN 7.21. Their identity with one another is uncertain even in DPPN. MN 100:4.2 assigns the mango grove to the Todeyya brahmins in the plural. AN 3.59, MN 99, SN 7.19–20 and SN 46.54 are neighboring citation hits. AN 5.200, AN 10.122, SN 7.22 and SN 46.56 list Saṅgārava in chapter recaps.

saṅkha.notes: DN 26:24.1 names the future king of Ketumatī. In DN 26:26.1–2 Sujato renders Mahāpanāda's yūpa as a sacrificial post and lists ascetics, brahmins and people in need as recipients of the king's charity. DPPN describes a palace given to the Saṅgha. The plant sense has no candidate.

saṅkicca.notes: MN 36, MN 76 and AN 6.57 name the ascetic Kisa Saṅkicca alongside Nanda Vaccha and Gosāla. The candidate describes the Buddhist elder who speaks the forest verses of Thag 11.1. Attaching his biography to Kisa's sense would conflate them.

sela.notes: MN 92:6.2 and Snp 3.7:6.2 give Sela an escort of three hundred students. DPPN says 250. Thag 16.6 also gives three hundred. MN 91 and MN 93 are adjacent citation hits. The hits in SN 5.9 and Thig 3.7 belong to the nun Selā.

selā.notes: Thig 3.7 attributes the verses about sensual pleasure to Selā. SN 5.1 has parallel verses under Āḷavikā. In SN 5.9 the nun named Selā answers Māra's question about the origin of the puppet. SN 5.8 concerns Sīsupacālā and SN 5.10 concerns Vajirā, with Selā named in its chapter recap. MN 92, Snp 3.7 and Thag 16.6 concern the male brahmin Sela.

seniya.notes: MN 57:2.1 identifies the naked ascetic by his dog observance. All nine other packet suttas use Seniya for King Bimbisāra of Magadha. The citation also lands in MN 56, the discourse with Upāli.

serī.notes: SN 2.23 names the godling Serī. At 8.1 the Pali spells his former name as king sirī, which Sujato renders Serī. SN 2.21 and SN 2.22 concern Siva and Khema. The packet misses Serī in the chapter recap at SN 2.30:18.1.

seta.notes: SN 2.30:16.3 names the Himalayan peak. SN 3.1 is an adjacent citation hit. AN 6.43:3.1 explicitly calls Pasenadi's elephant seto nāma nāgo. Sujato translates the name as “White”, so the packet misses the elephant's discourse.

sikhāmoggallāna.notes: AN 4.234 names the brahmin who reports Soṇakāyana's claim about deeds. AN 4.233 is the preceding discourse.

sikhī.notes: DN 14 and SN 12.5 explicitly call Sikhī a fully awakened Buddha. Thag 7.5:4.2 also names him, one segment before his name appears in the English. The SN page range includes discourses on other Buddhas, with Sikhī also in the recap at SN 12.10:8.2. MN 116:6.26 lists a distinct independent Buddha for whom the packet has no entry.

sirivaḍḍha.notes: MN 88 names Pasenadi's minister. In SN 47.29 the sick householder tells Ānanda he has already abandoned the five lower fetters. Thag 1.41 names the elder and describes the storm at Vebhāra and Paṇḍava. MN 87 and SN 47.28 are adjacent citation hits. SN 47.30 concerns Mānadinna and mentions Sirivaḍḍha only in the recap of SN 47.29. The recap at Thag 1.50:2.1 spells the elder's name Sirīvaḍḍho.

siva.notes: SN 2.21:1.3 explicitly calls the visitor sivo devaputto. Sujato spells the name Shiva, and the packet reports zero mentions. The Pali recap at SN 2.30:18.1 also names him. SN 2.20 concerns Anāthapiṇḍika.

sobha.notes: DN 14:1.12.16 names Sobha as the reigning king in Koṇāgamana's time.

sobhavatī.notes: DN 14:1.12.17 identifies Sobhavatī as King Sobha's capital. Koṇāgamana's birthplace is a further detail in DPPN.

sobhita.notes: DPD and DPPN read sobhito in the list of independent Buddhas at MN 116:6.35 as a name. Sujato reads it as “beautiful”, describing Mānatthaddha. MN 116 is absent from the packet's allowed list, and MN 117 is an adjacent citation hit. AN 1.227 names the monk foremost in recollecting past lives, and in Thag 2.23 he recalls five hundred eons. The adjacent AN 1.235–247 and 1.248–257 groups miss him. Thag 2.30:3.2 also names him in the recap. The previous fully awakened Buddha has no candidate.

somā.notes: SN 5.2 and Thig 3.8 give the nun's reply to Māra on womanhood. SN 5.10:8.1 also names her in the recap. MN 90 identifies the lady at court by her sister Sakulā and their message through Pasenadi. DPPN calls Somā queen and DPD calls her the queen's sister. MN 90 does not settle her royal title. The English list in AN 8.91–117 includes Somā, but the local Pali goes straight from Khemā to Rucī, and the list gives no link to Sakulā. DN 13 invokes the god Soma. SN 5.1, SN 5.3, MN 89, AN 8.89 and AN 8.90 are neighboring citation hits.

sorata.notes: MN 116:6.20 names Sorata with Asayha and Khemābhirata in the list of independent Buddhas.

sotthija.notes: DN 14:1.11.5 names Sotthija as Koṇāgamana's chief attendant.

sovīra.notes: DN 19:36.6 gives Roruka to the Sovīras in the division of the kingdoms. The verse establishes the ancient identification. The modern locations proposed in DPD and DPPN differ.

soṇa.notes: The harp lesson in AN 6.55 recurs in Koḷivisa's own verse at Thag 13.1:7.3, so senses 1 and 5 share his entry. AN 1.205 names Koḷivisa for energy and AN 1.206 names Kuṭikaṇṇa for enunciation. Their shared file an1.198-208 cannot take a single identification. The other two cited AN 1 groups miss both monks. DN 14:1.9.3 names Vessabhū's disciple in the compound soṇuttaraṁ. SN 22.49, SN 22.50 and SN 35.128 identify Soṇa as gahapatiputta at Rājagaha. DPD's SN 22.44 and the mapped SN 22.48, SN 35.127 and SN 35.129 concern other subjects. Thag 2.37 names a further elder, Soṇa Poṭiriya, with no candidate. AN 1.241 and Thig 5.8 name the nun Soṇā. AN 8.91–117 lists the laywoman Soṇā and her mother. The packet also misses the chapter recaps at AN 6.64:14.1, SN 35.133:8.2, Thag 5.12:7.2 and Ud 5.10:5.3.

soṇadaṇḍa.notes: DN 4 names the brahmin granted Campā by Bimbisāra. He takes refuge at DN 4:24.4–5 and later asks about greeting the Buddha in public because his wealth depends on his reputation. DPPN's suggestion about the extent of his conversion is an inference.
